title: What Burndown Charts Miss About Real Software Delivery
partialText: This article argues that common software-delivery metrics such as burndown charts, velocity tracking, and percentage-complete estimates misrepresent how software is actually built. Because development is exploratory, nonlinear, and shaped by discovery, the author contends that demos, narratives, and shipped outcomes provide a more accurate picture of progress than process metrics designed primarily for reporting and stakeholder communication

title: Platform Engineering Will Eat Software Engineering and That's a Good Thing
partialText: This article argues that platform engineering is evolving from a specialized infrastructure discipline into the context in which modern software development happens. As AI workloads, internal developer platforms, and self-service infrastructure become essential to product delivery, platform teams increasingly determine what organizations can build and ship. The author contends that platform engineering now has direct business impact and should be viewed as a strategic function rather than a support role.

title: How to Architect a Scalable AI Tech Stack
partialText: This article provides an overview of the modern AI tech stack, breaking it down into data, model, and application layers. It explores the infrastructure required to build, deploy, and maintain AI systems, with particular attention to Generative AI, vector databases, MLOps tooling, model serving, and cloud-native architectures. The guide also examines emerging trends such as multimodal AI, edge deployment, AutoML, and responsible AI practices.

title: Your MVP Is Probably Too Big
partialText:
Building a smaller MVP is not about cutting corners. It is about testing one real assumption before you build everything else.
Most founders overbuild because launching something small feels uncomfortable, not because the extra features are actually needed.
If you removed half your planned features and the core promise still held up, you probably should.

title: Faster Code Generation Doesn't Guarantee Faster Software Delivery
partialText: AI Coding Assistants can help developers write code faster, but real team speed depends on review quality, code ownership, testing habits, and clear workflow rules.

title: The Radiology Shortage Is a Coordination Problem Disguised as a Hiring Problem
partialText: Radiology is still organized around a one-study, one-radiologist workflow that no longer scales with growing imaging demand and rising complexity. Other industries solved similar problems by shifting from individual execution to coordinated infrastructure. The future of radiology may depend less on adding more specialists and more on redesigning how diagnostic work is distributed, reviewed, and assembled.

title: 7 of the Best Voice Agent Testing Platforms in 2026
partialText: 42% of voice agent failures happen at the audio layer – invisible to generic LLM evals. This guide compares seven platforms built to test what transcript-only evaluation misses. Pick based on your build stage, not hype.

title: What Production-Grade RAG Evaluation Should Look Like
partialText: This article argues that evaluating agentic RAG systems requires far more than a single faithfulness score. It explores a production-focused evaluation stack built around RAGAS component metrics, node-level observability with LangSmith and Langfuse, critic scoring, retrieval-round analysis, latency and cost monitoring, and carefully curated evaluation datasets. The central thesis is that modern RAG systems fail in many ways that end-to-end metrics alone cannot detect.

title: Deploying On-Device AI Guardrails With Docker 29.1 and Spanner Omni
partialText: Shifting AI to the edge solves latency and privacy issues but creates a governance nightmare. This technical deep dive explores how backend engineers can use Docker Engine 29.1 and Google Spanner Omni to run SLMs locally, enforce strict Java-based safety guardrails, and maintain globally synchronized compliance logs.

title: The Cloud Data Leak: Architecting SQL to Stop Financial Bleeding
partialText: Cloud storage may be cheap, but processing, moving, and managing data often isn't. This article examines seven common architectural patterns that inflate cloud bills, including small-file fragmentation, cross-region joins, excessive retention windows, poor storage tiering, and unrestricted queries. It argues that modern data engineers must think like FinOps practitioners, optimizing not just for performance and scale but also for long-term infrastructure economics.

title: Building a Procedural Compliance Auditor With NVIDIA Nemotron and VSS
partialText: This tutorial demonstrates how to build a production-ready procedural compliance auditor using NVIDIA Nemotron Omni, vLLM, and the NVIDIA VSS Blueprint. Using HVAC installations as a case study, the system combines multimodal video analysis, document retrieval, self-consistency scoring, and structured reporting to evaluate whether field technicians follow prescribed procedures. The architecture generalizes to any industry where video evidence must be audited against documented processes.

title: Developer Farm Earns a 67.56 Proof of Usefulness Score by Building an Honest AI Architecture
partialText: In this Proof of Usefulness interview, Illya Rochev explains how Developer Farm tackles Goodhart’s Law in AI-assisted software development. The framework separates planning, execution, and verification into isolated layers, preventing coding agents from seeing tests or acceptance criteria. The goal is to produce solutions that solve business problems rather than simply optimizing for passing evaluations, while maintaining extremely low operating costs through local model execution.

title: AI Coding Agents Need Evidence Packs, Not Just Final Answers
partialText: Agent Blackbox is an open-source, local-first CLI that records what AI coding agents actually do rather than relying on their final summaries. By capturing terminal output, git diffs, test results, policy violations, event timelines, and audit logs, it creates evidence packs that make agent runs reviewable and easier to trust. The article argues that as coding agents gain more autonomy, auditability and observability will become essential developer infrastructure.

title: From Telecom to AI-Driven Supply Chains: How Marceu Martins Applies ‘Trust Architectures’
partialText: Drawing on decades of experience across telecommunications, manufacturing, and supply-chain systems, Marceu Martins advocates for "trust architecture" as a framework for governing autonomous AI systems. The article explores how reliability, compliance, human oversight, and operational guardrails can help ensure that AI-driven decisions remain predictable and accountable, particularly in environments where software actions have real-world consequences.

title: RTSP Refuses To Die Because It Still Works Just Fine
partialText: Despite frequent predictions of its demise, RTSP remains a foundational protocol for video ingest across IP cameras, surveillance systems, industrial monitoring, drones, and other hardware-heavy environments. This article explains RTSP's architecture, its relationship with RTP and RTCP, its security considerations, and its role within modern streaming pipelines. It argues that RTSP persists not because of inertia, but because it continues to solve specific low-latency, hardware-interoperability problems better than many newer alternatives

title: AI 3D Generation in Production: Real Workflow Results from Game, Hardware, and Print Studios

title: Your Asset Performance Management Software Is Only as Good as Your Data
partialText: Many organizations treat asset performance management as a software problem when it is fundamentally a data problem. This article explores why APM platforms depend on complete, consistent, traceable, and timely data to generate trustworthy predictions. It argues that fragmented source systems, poor master data, weak lineage, and legacy infrastructure are the primary causes of underperforming APM initiatives, and advocates for a data-first approach that prioritizes governance, integration, and operational trust before platform selection

title: Technology Rules Look Different Once Real Systems Are Involved
partialText: Technology policies may look straightforward on paper, but real-world implementation introduces challenges around compliance, usability, reliability, and long-term system behavior.
